title: The Man Who Wrote Mueller’s Rules

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日简报

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: Dealbook的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市Dealbook峰会的现场采访一些商界、政界和文化界最有影响力的领袖，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 我们将于11月18日在nytimes.com上现场直播精选采访，供所有人

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你会收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: The investigation that Robert Mueller has conducted as special counsel is based on a set of rules designed to allow for the investigation of a sitting president.
sentences.zh: 罗伯特·穆勒作为特别检察官进行的调查，是基于一套旨在允许调查在任总统的规则。

sentences.en: Those rules will now be tested.
sentences.zh: 这些规则现在将接受考验。

sentences.en: It's Thursday, August 23rd.
sentences.zh: 今天是8月23日，星期四。

sentences.en: From the time the founders sat down and created the documents and the constitution that this
sentences.zh: 从开国元勋们坐下来创建这个国家所依据的文件和宪法的那一刻起，

sentences.en: country is based on, they knew there would be this incredibly difficult question that the country would have to wrestle with, which was how would the government investigate itself?
sentences.zh: 他们就知道国家将不得不面对一个极其艰难的问题，那就是政府将如何调查自身？

sentences.en: And in particular, how would the government investigate the president?
sentences.zh: 尤其是，政府将如何调查总统？

sentences.en: It was not clear.
sentences.zh: 当时并不清楚。

sentences.en: And over our history at three distinct points, we've seen this tested.
sentences.zh: 在我们历史上的三个不同时期，我们都看到了这一点受到考验。

sentences.en: Nixon, Clinton, and now Trump.
sentences.zh: 尼克松、克林顿，现在是特朗普。

sentences.en: Mike Schmidt, take us back to the first time that this was tested.
sentences.zh: 迈克·施密特，带我们回溯到这第一次受到考验的时候。

sentences.en: What was it that prompted the investigation into Richard Nixon?
sentences.zh: 是什么促成了对理查德·尼克松的调查？

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: We have a mystery story out of Washington.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿传来了一个神秘的故事。

sentences.en: In 1972, burglars broke into the headquarters of the Democratic National Committee in the Watergate Hotel in Washington.
sentences.zh: 1972年，江洋大盗闯入了华盛顿水门酒店的民主党全国委员会总部。

sentences.en: Mr. Nixon says emphatically that the White House is in no way involved in the burglary and bugging of the Democratic headquarters, and he'll have no further comment on that matter.
sentences.zh: 尼克松先生明确表示，白宫绝未参与对民主党总部的江洋大盗和窃听活动，对此他将不再做进一步评论。

sentences.en: This leads to questions about the involvement of the president, and it needs to be investigated.
sentences.zh: 这引发了对总统是否涉案的质疑，因而需要展开调查。

sentences.en: There's still another
sentences.zh: 还有另一个

sentences.en: Watergate investigation in the offing, the one to be conducted by a special prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 即将开展的水门事件调查，将由特别检察官进行。

sentences.en: The Justice
sentences.zh: 司法

sentences.en: Department ultimately appoints a special prosecutor.
sentences.zh: 部最终任命了一名特别检察官。

sentences.en: He is Archibald Cox.
sentences.zh: 他就是阿奇博尔德·考克斯。

sentences.en: An investigator who is supposed to be protected from outside politics to look into the burglary.
sentences.zh: 一位本应受到保护、免受外部政治干扰以调查江洋大盗案的调查员。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 大家晚上好。

sentences.en: The country tonight is in the midst of what may be the most serious constitutional crisis in its history.
sentences.zh: 今晚的国家正处于其历史上或许最严重的宪政危机之中。

sentences.en: What happens is that along the way in that investigation, Nixon fires Archibald Cox in the Saturday Night Massacre.
sentences.zh: 在调查的过程中，尼克松在“星期六之夜大屠杀”中解雇了阿奇博尔德·考克斯。

sentences.en: All of this adds up to a totally unprecedented situation, a grave and profound crisis in which the president has set himself against his own attorney general in the
sentences.zh: 所有这一切汇聚成了一种完全前所未有的局面，一场严峻而深重的危机，总统将自己置于其自身的总检察长和

sentences.en: Department of Justice.
sentences.zh: 司法部的对立面。

sentences.en: And there are questions about whether the White House, the president and his aides interfered with the work of investigators.
sentences.zh: 并且有人质疑白宫、总统及其助手是否干预了调查人员的工作。

sentences.en: Nothing like this has ever happened before.
sentences.zh: 从未发生过类似的事情。

sentences.en: So in the aftermath of Watergate, there's a deep fear within the country about how power of the presidency can be abused.
sentences.zh: 因此，在水门事件之后，全国上下对总统权力可能被滥用深感恐惧。

sentences.en: And as the country wrestles with that, Congress comes up with a system that they say will ensure the things that went on under Nixon will not happen again.
sentences.zh: 正当国家为此苦苦挣扎时，国会提出了一套他们认为能确保尼克松时期发生的事情不会重演的制度。

sentences.en: That there will be a way for investigators to have special protections to keep them completely free of political influence from the White House.
sentences.zh: 这将为调查人员提供特殊保护，使其彻底摆脱来自白宫的政治影响。

sentences.en: The independent counsel statute.
sentences.zh: 独立检察官法案。

sentences.en: It essentially creates a fourth branch of government that allows Congress or the attorney general to appoint someone to look into the president.
sentences.zh: 它本质上创建了政府的第四个分支，允许国会或总检察长任命某人来调查总统。

sentences.en: And the investigators are protected at the highest levels.
sentences.zh: 而且调查人员在最高层面上受到保护。

sentences.en: It's very, very difficult to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 要摆脱他们非常非常困难。

sentences.en: They essentially report to themselves.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上只对自己负责。

sentences.en: They can take all sorts of action on their own, like bringing cases or sending information to Congress.
sentences.zh: 他们可以自行采取各种行动，比如提起诉讼或向国会提交信息。

sentences.en: It gives them almost carte blanche in terms of investigation.
sentences.zh: 在调查方面，这几乎赋予了他们全权委托。

sentences.en: So how does this new system work out?
sentences.zh: 那么这个新系统效果如何呢？

sentences.en: After the laws pass, every president has to confront one of these Carter with a scandal involving Studio 54, Reagan with Iran-Contra, which bleeds into George H.W.
sentences.zh: 法律通过后，每位总统都必须应对其中之一：卡特面临涉及54号工作室的丑闻，里根面临伊朗门事件，该事件蔓延到了老布什

sentences.en: Bush's administration.
sentences.zh: 政府。

sentences.en: And then we get to Clinton.
sentences.zh: 然后我们来到了克林顿时期。

sentences.en: With Clinton, an independent counsel is appointed to look into an Arkansas land deal called Whitewater.
sentences.zh: 在克林顿任上，任命了一名独立检察官来调查名为“白水事件”的阿肯色州土地交易。

sentences.en: The greatest discrepancy between what the White House has claimed and what journalists are uncovering in the
sentences.zh: 白宫所声称的与记者在所谓的白水事件中

sentences.en: so-called Whitewater affair lies in the amount of money that Bill and Hillary Clinton say they lost on that land investment deal.
sentences.zh: 所揭露的之间最大的出入，在于比尔和希拉里·克林顿声称他们在那个土地投资交易中损失的金额。

sentences.en: And an investigation that begins looking at this deal.
sentences.zh: 而一项开始调查此交易的调查。

sentences.en: CNN has confirmed that Whitewater counsel Kenneth Starr has been granted permission to expand his investigation.
sentences.zh: 美国有线电视新闻网已证实，白水事件检察官肯尼斯·斯塔尔已获准扩大调查范围。

sentences.en: Turns into one about the president's sexual relationship with a White House intern.
sentences.zh: 变成了一起关于总统与白宫实习生性关系的调查。

sentences.en: We've had enough of the public inquiries into the deepest private matters of this president and the people around him.
sentences.zh: 我们已经受够了对这位总统及其身边人最深层私人事务的公开质询。

sentences.en: We've had enough of the unchecked special prosecutor and his unlimited spending of taxpayers' money.
sentences.zh: 我们已经受够了不受制衡的特别检察官及其对纳税人金钱的无限挥霍。

sentences.en: It's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这非常困难。

sentences.en: It's almost a form of McCarthyism, if you will.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，这几乎是一种麦卡锡主义的形式。

sentences.en: So in the aftermath of Nixon, the country had essentially built a moat around the investigators who were going to look at the president.
sentences.zh: 因此，在尼克松事件之后，国家基本上在将要调查总统的调查人员周围建立了一条护城河。

sentences.en: And by the time we get to Clinton, the country says,
sentences.zh: 而到了克林顿时期，国家说，

sentences.en: wow, that moat is so big and so treacherous that we can't even get to the investigators.
sentences.zh: 哇，这条护城河是如此之大且充满险阻，我们甚至无法接近调查人员。

sentences.en: They're just off on their own doing whatever they want.
sentences.zh: 他们只是自顾自地做他们想做的事。

sentences.en: We're not comfortable with that.
sentences.zh: 我们对此感到很不自在。

sentences.en: So in correcting for the sense during the Nixon era that the prosecutor was too beholden to the president, there was a sense that there had been an overcorrection.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了纠正尼克松时期那种检察官过分听命于总统的感觉，人们认为之前矫枉过正了。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in the wake of the Starr report, the Justice Department is once again confronted with the question of what should these investigations look like?
sentences.zh: 因此，在斯塔尔报告发布后，司法部再次面临这些调查应该是什么样子的质问。

sentences.en: And a group is formed to try and answer that question.
sentences.zh: 并成立了一个小组来试图回答这个问题。

sentences.en: The person leading it is a 20-something lawyer named Neil Katyal.
sentences.zh: 领导它的是一位二十多岁的律师，名叫尼尔·卡蒂亚尔。

sentences.en: My very first assignment at the Justice Department as a young pup, I was 27 years old,
sentences.zh: 我在司法部的第一项工作，作为一个乳臭未干、年仅27岁的年轻人，

sentences.en: was to examine the way in which high-level executive branch wrongdoing should be investigated and ultimately prosecuted.
sentences.zh: 就是审查高级行政部门违规行为应该如何被调查并最终被起诉的方式。

sentences.en: So it was your job to figure out what investigations of presidents should look like after the Ken Starr investigation.
sentences.zh: 所以你的工作是弄清楚肯·斯塔尔调查之后，对总统的调查应该是什么样子。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Today, Neil is a very well-known lawyer in Washington who's argued dozens of cases before the Supreme Court,
sentences.zh: 如今，尼尔是华盛顿一位非常知名的律师，曾在最高法院辩论过数十起案件，

sentences.en: was the acting solicitor general under President Obama, and most recently argued against the travel ban case before the court.
sentences.zh: 曾任奥巴马总统时期的代理副总检察长，最近还在最高法院对抗了旅行禁令案。

sentences.en: But back then, he was sort of this wide-eyed, whip-smart lawyer working for Janet Reno, the attorney general at the Justice Department.
sentences.zh: 但在当年，他有点像是在司法部总检察长珍妮特·雷诺手下工作的那种目光纯真、精明强干的律师。

sentences.en: So soon after I got to the Justice Department, it became pretty clear that we needed to think through what the alternative to the Independent Counsel Act would be.
sentences.zh: 所以自我进入司法部后不久，就很清楚我们需要仔细考虑独立检察官法案的替代方案会是什么。

sentences.en: We definitely didn't want to repeat the sins of the old model.
sentences.zh: 我们绝对不想重蹈旧模式的覆辙。

sentences.en: At the same time, we recognized that, you know, when the president is under investigation or someone close to him, it can't be treated just like a normal investigation,
sentences.zh: 与此同时，我们认识到，你知道的，当总统或与其亲近的人正在接受调查时，它不能被当作普通调查来对待，

sentences.en: because after all, the president has all sorts of powers to interfere with an investigation.
sentences.zh: 因为毕竟总统拥有各种干预调查的权力。

sentences.en: All of these were kinds of concerns that said we need to have some way to investigate high-level executive branch wrongdoing.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是各种顾虑，表明我们需要某种方式来调查高级行政部门的违规行为。

sentences.en: It just doesn't need to go so far as the Independent Counsel Act did.
sentences.zh: 只是它不需要像独立检察官法案那样走得那么远。

sentences.en: I wonder if you could just give us your philosophy of developing a system around how to best investigate a sitting president.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你是否能给我们讲讲你围绕如何最好地调查在任总统来开发一个系统的哲学。

sentences.en: What do you think is at the heart of making that successful?
sentences.zh: 你认为使之成功核心是什么？

sentences.en: The heart is one very simple thing, which is that you have two values that we both love and that sound great in isolation, but that are mutually exclusive with one another.
sentences.zh: 核心是非常简单的一点，那就是你有两个我们都热爱且在孤立状态下听起来很棒，但却彼此排斥的价值观。

sentences.en: And those values are popular accountability and independence.
sentences.zh: 这两个价值观就是民意问责与独立性。

sentences.en: So we like the idea of an independent investigation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们喜欢独立调查的想法。

sentences.en: We like the idea that, you know, high-level wrongdoing is going to be policed.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢这样的想法，你知道的，高级别的违规行为将受到监管。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: But we also like the idea of accountability, because what happens if the prosecutor herself or himself strays and is acting wrongly?
sentences.zh: 但我们也喜欢问责制，因为如果检察官本人误入歧途并有不当行为会怎么样？

sentences.en: We want them to be accountable in some way, too.
sentences.zh: 我们也希望他们在某种程度上受到问责。

sentences.en: The problem is that the more independent you make a prosecutor, the less accountable you make her, and vice versa.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，你把检察官独立性做得越高，赋予她的问责性就越少，反之亦然。

sentences.en: And so the philosophy was to try and strike that balance much more in the middle than on one side or the other.
sentences.zh: 因此，这一哲学的目的是试图将这种平衡更多地拉向中间，而不是偏向任何一端。

sentences.en: So what do they come up with?
sentences.zh: 那么他们想出了什么办法？

sentences.en: They come up with a third way forward, the special counsel regulation.
sentences.zh: 他们想出了前进的第三条道路，即特别检察官条例。

sentences.en: So the special counsel regulations did away with the Independent Counsel Act and replaced it with
sentences.zh: 因此，特别检察官条例废除了独立检察官法案，并将其替换为

sentences.en: a prosecutor housed within the Justice Department itself, and indeed ultimately accountable to the
sentences.zh: 一个安置在司法部内部的检察官，并且最终确实对

sentences.en: Justice Department leadership.
sentences.zh: 司法部领导层负责。

sentences.en: So in the new model you created, you're responding to Starr and also pulling on the lessons of the Nixon structure, and you sort of ultimately end up
sentences.zh: 所以在你创建的新模式中，你是在回应斯塔尔，同时也借鉴了尼克松体制的教训，你最终基本上

sentences.en: leaning in the direction of what had been in place under Nixon.
sentences.zh: 倾向于尼克松时期曾存在过的那种方向。

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: What we decided on was something that looked very much like ultimately what we got with Nixon and Watergate, which is special regulations that create a prosecutor who has
sentences.zh: 我们决定采用的方案在很大程度上看起来最终就像我们在尼克松和水门事件中得到的方案一样，即特殊的规章制度，创造出这样一位检察官：他在履行职责时拥有

sentences.en: day-to-day independence in carrying out his duties, but ultimately has to go get permission from the
sentences.zh: 日常的独立性，但最终必须就任何在任何方面偏离司法部政策和协议的实质性步骤向

sentences.en: Attorney General for any substantial step that deviates in any way from Justice Department policies and protocols.
sentences.zh: 总检察长寻求批准。

sentences.en: And that's the system we're currently living under, right?
sentences.zh: 这就是我们目前生活于其中的系统，对吧？

sentences.en: This one created by
sentences.zh: 这个由

sentences.en: Neil Katyal that attempts to learn the lessons of these past two presidential investigations that are both seen as flawed and these kind of two poles.
sentences.zh: 尼尔·卡蒂亚尔创建的系统，试图汲取这两次都被视为有缺陷且处于这两种极端的前总统调查的教训。

sentences.en: Yes, and that's the one that Donald Trump is confronting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是唐纳德·特朗普正在面对的系统。

sentences.en: The thing is, is that the system, since Neil created it, had not really been tested.
sentences.zh: 问题是，这个系统自尼尔创建以来，并没有真正受到过考验。

sentences.en: This is the first sort of run of it.
sentences.zh: 这是它的首次某种意义上的运行。

sentences.en: You know, certainly you can have unprecedented things happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当然可能会发生前所未有事情。

sentences.en: You know, we knew that when we were writing the regulations, things we couldn't even anticipate.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们在撰写规章时就知道这一点，有些甚至是 我们无法预料的。

sentences.en: And so there had to be some flexibility in the regulations to say, well, you can't just always blindly follow what has gone before.
sentences.zh: 因此，规章中必须留有一些灵活性，以表明，好吧，你不能总是盲目地遵循过去发生的事情。

sentences.en: Sometimes you'll need to deviate from policy and practice.
sentences.zh: 有时你需要偏离政策和惯例。

sentences.en: And while this all sounds abstract, the way I'm explaining it, I'm about to make it very concrete.
sentences.zh: 虽然这一切听起来很抽象，就像我解释的那样，但我马上要把它变得非常具体。

sentences.en: There is a whole debate right now about whether a sitting president like Donald Trump can be indicted.
sentences.zh: 现在正围绕着像唐纳德·特朗普这样的在任总统是否可以被起诉展开一场大辩论。

sentences.en: And there are two Justice
sentences.zh: 有两项司法

sentences.en: Department policy opinions, which suggest that a sitting president cannot be indicted and tried while in office.
sentences.zh: 部政策意见，表明在任总统在职期间不能被起诉和审判。

sentences.en: Ordinarily, a special counsel would be bound by those policies and couldn't indict, for example, Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，特别检察官将受这些政策约束，因此无法起诉例如唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: So Mueller wouldn't be able to.
sentences.zh: 所以穆勒将无法这样做。

sentences.en: But in the special counsel regulations, we anticipated for the possibility that something unusual might happen.
sentences.zh: 但在特别检察官条例中，我们预料到了可能会发生一些不寻常事情的可能性。

sentences.en: And there's a mechanism for
sentences.zh: 并且有一种机制供

sentences.en: Mr. Mueller to go and seek the indictment, which is to go and ask the acting attorney general,
sentences.zh: 穆勒先生去寻求起诉，那就是去请求代理总检察长

sentences.en: Rod Rosenstein, for permission to do so.
sentences.zh: 罗德·罗森斯坦批准这样做。

sentences.en: Now, if Rod says yes, the criminal process will unfold against the president.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果罗德说可以，针对总统的刑事诉讼程序将会展开。

sentences.en: If Rod Rosenstein says no, that triggers a report to Congress.
sentences.zh: 如果罗德·罗森斯坦说不，那将触发向国会提交报告。

sentences.en: And it's a mandatory report at that level.
sentences.zh: 而且那是该层级的一份强制性报告。

sentences.en: And then Rosenstein and Mueller have to explain what happened to Congress.
sentences.zh: 然后罗森斯坦和穆勒必须向国会解释发生了什么。

sentences.en: And that then provides sunlight into the process.
sentences.zh: 这随后为整个过程带来了阳光（透明度）。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that in order to bring oversight and sunlight into this investigation, something that would be a politically tinged thing, you put something in there
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，为了给这项调查带来监督和阳光，这是一件带有政治色彩的事情，你在其中加入了一些内容：

sentences.en: that if there had been a disagreement within the Justice Department where the prosecutor wanted to do
sentences.zh: 如果司法部内部出现分歧，检察官想做

sentences.en: something, but the political people running it said no, Congress would have a way of finding out about it.
sentences.zh: 某事，但负责运营的政治人员说不，国会将有一种方法能够查明此事。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: We had to worry that the attorney general is, after all, the president's guy.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不担心总检察长毕竟是总统的人。

sentences.en: Or here, the acting attorney general, Rod Rosenstein, is the president's guy.
sentences.zh: 或者在这里，代理总检察长罗德·罗森斯坦是总统的人。

sentences.en: He was put in place by
sentences.zh: 他是被

sentences.en: President Trump.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统安插的。

sentences.en: He is a Trump nominee.
sentences.zh: 他是特朗普提名的候选人。

sentences.en: And so you always have to worry, is that person going to act based on party politics or act on the basis of principle?
sentences.zh: 所以你总是不得不担心，那个人会根据党派政治行事，还是会根据原则行事？

sentences.en: And on the off chance that they were going to do the former party politics and try and stymie an investigation or say no to a special
sentences.zh: 而在他们万一要做出前者（党派政治）并试图阻挠调查或对像穆勒这样的特别

sentences.en: counsel like Mueller, that triggered a report to Congress.
sentences.zh: 检察官说不的极少数情况下，那将触发一份提交给国会的报告。

sentences.en: And here, if Mueller asks Rosenstein to indict the president and Rosenstein says no, that triggers a mandatory report.
sentences.zh: 这里，如果穆勒要求罗森斯坦起诉总统而罗森斯坦拒绝，就会触发强制报告机制。

sentences.en: And by providing those reports, ultimately, the media also would be involved and popular accountability would be enhanced by people like yourselves writing about what was going on.
sentences.zh: 通过提供这些报告，最终媒体也会卷入其中，而像诸位这样撰文报道进展的人，也将提升公众的问责力度。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So Neil builds in this kind of backstop where if the prosecutor finds evidence of crimes,
sentences.zh: 所以尼尔设置了这样一种后盾机制，即如果检察官发现了犯罪证据，

sentences.en: for example, Congress would definitely find out about it, even if the political appointees like
sentences.zh: 例如，国会肯定会知情，哪怕效力于总统的政治任命官员——

sentences.en: the attorney general who works for the president tried to squash it because that dispute between the prosecutor and the attorney general would become public to Congress.
sentences.zh: 比如听命于总统的司法部长试图将其压下去，因为检察官与司法部长之间的分歧会公开到国会层面。

sentences.en: So if there is an effort by the political leaders of the Justice Department to smother part of the investigation, Congress will find out about it.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果司法部的政治领导层试图掩盖部分调查，国会将会有所察觉。

sentences.en: That will be the check.
sentences.zh: 这将成为一种制衡。

sentences.en: Neil thinks it's working, but he also acknowledges that this is the nightmare scenario he dreamed up when he put these regulations together.
sentences.zh: 尼尔认为它正在发挥作用，但他也承认，这是他当年制定这些规章时构想出的噩梦般的场景。

sentences.en: We imagined it, but it was the nightmare scenario.
sentences.zh: 我们当时设想过，但这确实是最坏的噩梦场景。

sentences.en: We were writing at a time in the shadow of Nixon.
sentences.zh: 我们写作的时代正笼罩在尼克松事件的阴影之下。

sentences.en: So we understood the possibility that you could have a president who was alleged to be deeply corrupt and deeply antithetical to the rule of law.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们深知这样一种可能性：可能会出现一位被指控严重腐败且极度违背法治精神的总统。

sentences.en: I sure hoped that it would never be something I'd see in my lifetime and that the country wouldn't see.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望这永远不会是我有生之年能看到的，也是国家不曾经历的。

sentences.en: But we wrote for that possibility.
sentences.zh: 但我们正是为了这种可能性而撰写了这些规章。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that what is playing out today is along the lines of the nightmare scenario
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，今天正在上演的一切，正符合当年你在司法部时，

sentences.en: you, as a young lawyer in your 20s, imagined at the Justice Department when you created the structure that the president's being investigated under today.
sentences.zh: 作为一个二十多岁的年轻律师所构想的噩梦场景，也就是总统目前正面临调查的这套体制。

sentences.en: Yes, we hoped like heck it wouldn't happen, but it was a black swan event that we had to write regulations to deal with.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们极其希望它不会发生，但这属于黑天鹅事件，我们必须通过制定规章来应对。

sentences.en: And that's what these regulations were crafted for, something like today.
sentences.zh: 这些规章就是为了类似于今天的这种局面而量身打造的。

sentences.en: So when Neil says that this is the nightmare situation, what's nightmarish about it is that he hoped Congress would be this kind of fail safe in this system he created.
sentences.zh: 因此，当尼尔说这是最坏的噩梦时，可怕之处在于他曾希望国会能在他创建的这个体制中扮演安全网的角色。

sentences.en: And we now have a Congress that doesn't seem necessarily prepared to play that role.
sentences.zh: 而我们现在看到的国会，似乎并未准备好扮演这个角色。

sentences.en: Well, if you build a system that's based on using the checks and balances, and one of the three branches has shown itself to not be particularly interested in overseeing
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你构建了一个基于权力制衡的体制，而三个分支之一已经表现得对监督

sentences.en: another one of them, then you are a bit concerned that that backstop that you're relying on may not be there to keep the entire system together.
sentences.zh: 另一个分支兴趣索然，那么你难免会有些担心，你所依赖的那个后盾可能无法继续维持整个体制的运转。

sentences.en: Congress is the backstop and he thinks Congress will keep it on track.
sentences.zh: 国会就是后盾，他认为国会会让事情步入正轨。

sentences.en: But this is a Congress that has been enormously loyal to the president and not been particularly interested in conducting oversight of the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 但如今的这个国会一直对总统极其忠诚，对监督行政分支并没有什么兴趣。

sentences.en: Well, I know that everyone has a certain amount of impatience about this, but I think it's really
sentences.zh: 好吧，我知道每个人对此都有点急不可耐，但我认为

sentences.en: wrong to think about a backstop failing or anything like that, because, you know, criminal cases and the criminal process takes a long time.
sentences.zh: 去设想什么后盾失效之类的观点是非常错误的，因为你知道，刑事案件和刑事诉讼需要很长时间。

sentences.en: And it's really only since yesterday that we've had really the first sustained set of allegations against the president sworn in federal court.
sentences.zh: 而且直到昨天，我们才真正迎来了在联邦法院宣誓后对总统的第一波持续指控。

sentences.en: And so I think it's too early to talk about failing or not.
sentences.zh: 因此，我认为现在谈论是否失效还为时过早。

sentences.en: I certainly hope that, you know, the Congress takes its responsibilities seriously, and I suspect that they will.
sentences.zh: 我当然希望国会能认真对待自己的职责，而且我猜他们会的。

sentences.en: Mike, what would Neil say to the idea that if Congress doesn't act in this case, that it's still not a failure of the backstop, this failsafe he set up, because Congress was
sentences.zh: 迈克，如果国会在本案中不采取行动，尼尔会怎么看待这种观点：即这依然不能算作后盾或他设置的安全网失效，因为国会是

sentences.en: democratically elected, and this is the will of the people.
sentences.zh: 民主选举产生的，而这就是人民的意志。

sentences.en: So really, the backstop in a representative democracy is the people.
sentences.zh: 所以说到底，代议制民主中的后盾其实就是人民。

sentences.en: And if they want a Congress that doesn't act against the president, who doesn't think this is a crime, then that's what they've gotten.
sentences.zh: 如果他们选出一个不对抗总统、不认为这是犯罪的国会，那么这就是他们应得的结果。

sentences.en: But from Neil's perspective, would that mean that the president could essentially live above the law?
sentences.zh: 但从尼尔的角度来看，这是否意味着总统实际上可以凌驾于法律之上？

sentences.en: That if the investigators found stuff that the president had done wrong, and you can't indict a
sentences.zh: 如果调查人员发现了总统的不当行为，而根据司法部的指导方针，你又不能起诉

sentences.en: president under the Department of Justice guidelines, and the only way of dealing with the president is
sentences.zh: 总统，处理总统的唯一途径

sentences.en: through impeachment, if investigators found that the president broke the law, and that information
sentences.zh: 只能通过弹劾，如果调查人员发现总统违法了，且这些信息

sentences.en: was given to Congress as the check and Congress ignored it, then you are allowing a president to live above the law.
sentences.zh: 作为制衡手段交给了国会，而国会却置之不理，那么你就是在纵容总统凌驾于法律之上。

sentences.en: But by Neil's definition of what makes this system work, would Congress have to act to prove that the system that he created actually functions?
sentences.zh: 但在尼尔对让这套体制运转起来的要素的定义中，国会是否必须采取行动，才能证明他所创建的体制确实在发挥作用？

sentences.en: Well, it depends on what the investigators want to do, and it depends on how the Justice
sentences.zh: 这取决于调查人员想做什么，也取决于司法部

sentences.en: Department handles it.
sentences.zh: 如何处理此事。

sentences.en: If the political leadership running the Justice Department agree with the moves that Bob Mueller and other investigators want to take, then you don't have an issue that
sentences.zh: 如果掌管司法部的政治领导层赞同鲍勃·穆勒和其他调查人员想要采取的行动，那么你就不会遇到

sentences.en: needs to be dealt with by Congress.
sentences.zh: 需要国会介入的问题。

sentences.en: It's only if there's a disagreement that Congress would get involved.
sentences.zh: 只有在出现分歧时，国会才会介入。

sentences.en: I think overcorrection is a natural part of the American experiment.
sentences.zh: 我认为矫枉过正本来就是美国政治实验中很自然的一部分。

sentences.en: We're often trying to solve the last problem, and, you know, it's to be expected that whenever you have a problem like Nixon, you try and
sentences.zh: 我们常常试图解决上一个问题，你知道，每当你遇到像尼克松这样的问题时，你就会

sentences.en: say to yourself, how do we make sure it never, ever happens again?
sentences.zh: 告诫自己，我们该如何确保这种情况绝不再发生？

sentences.en: And you can do that, but sometimes your solution has costs.
sentences.zh: 你可以这么做，但有时你的解决方案也是有代价的。

sentences.en: And that's what happened with the Independent Council Act.
sentences.zh: 独立检察官法案就是如此。

sentences.en: I sure hope that the special counsel regulations were not an overreaction to what was going on there, but, you know, time will tell about that, too.
sentences.zh: 我真诚地希望特别检察官条例不是对当时局势的过激反应，但你知道，时间会证明一切。

sentences.en: And I think we all have to have humility when we're dealing and designing something of this magnitude that we could have gotten it wrong.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当我们处理和设计如此规模的事务时，我们都必须保持谦逊，意识到我们可能会弄错。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is that we haven't gotten far enough in this story whether to say that the reaction to Starr was an overreaction?
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，对于针对斯塔尔的反应是否属于过激反应，我们现在下结论还为时尚早？

sentences.en: That's correct.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: I mean, we're only in, you know, Act Two of what I think is going to be a four or five act play here.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为我们目前正处于这场预计有四到五幕的戏剧的第二幕。

sentences.en: So I think, you know, time's going to tell.
sentences.zh: 所以我想时间会给出答案的。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the special counsel regulations so far have worked very well in protecting Mueller and providing accountability to his actions.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为到目前为止，特别检察官条例在保护穆勒以及对他的行动进行问责方面发挥得非常出色。

sentences.en: But now the rubber's about to hit the road.
sentences.zh: 但现在，真正的考验要开始了。

sentences.en: We're about to find out how truly independent is Mueller?
sentences.zh: 我们马上就要发现穆勒到底有多独立？

sentences.en: Is his job vulnerable?
sentences.zh: 他的职位是否岌岌可危？

sentences.en: Is the president going to try and fire him in one way or another?
sentences.zh: 总统是否会试图以某种方式解雇他？

sentences.en: Is there going to be interference with the investigation?
sentences.zh: 调查是否会受到干扰？

sentences.en: But I do think the regulations provide a framework for interference.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这些条例为应对干扰提供了一个框架。

sentences.en: And if the president takes any of those actions, either directly or indirectly, they're going to be reported to Congress, and then it'll be up to Congress to do its job.
sentences.zh: 如果总统直接或间接地采取了任何此类行动，都将报告给国会，接下来就轮到国会去履行职责了。

sentences.en: Mike, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 迈克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请我来。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他内容。

sentences.en: With that, I'll take your questions.
sentences.zh: 好了，接下来我来回答你们的问题。

sentences.en: Thank you, Sarah.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，萨拉。

sentences.en: Michael Cohen under oaths included guilty to, among things, paying Stormy Daniels and Karen McDougal during the campaign.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·科恩在宣誓后承认了多项罪名，其中包括在竞选期间向斯托米·丹尼尔斯和凯伦·麦克杜格尔支付封口费。

sentences.en: And he says he did it at the direction of the president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 并且他说他是听从美国总统的指示才这么做的。

sentences.en: Did President Trump commit a crime?
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统是否犯罪了？

sentences.en: As the president said, we've stated many times, he did nothing wrong.
sentences.zh: 正如总统所说，我们已经多次表态，他没有做错任何事。

sentences.en: There are no charges against him.
sentences.zh: 他没有面临任何指控。

sentences.en: And we've commented on this extensively.
sentences.zh: 我们对此已经做过充分的评论。

sentences.en: During a briefing at the White House on Wednesday, Press Secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders insisted that
sentences.zh: 周三在白宫举行的一场吹风会上，新闻秘书萨拉·赫卡比·桑德斯坚称，

sentences.en: President Trump's effort to silence two women who claimed to have had affairs with him did not violate the law, despite a guilty plea in the case by his lawyer, Michael Cohen.
sentences.zh: 尽管其律师迈克尔·科恩在该案中已认罪，但特朗普总统试图让两名声称与他有染的女性闭嘴的举动并未违法。

sentences.en: Can you stand here today and say the president has never lied to the American people?
sentences.zh: 你能站在这里说总统从来没有对美国人民撒过谎吗？

sentences.en: Because so many people now look back at that tape of him on Air Force One saying he knew nothing about these
sentences.zh: 因为现在有那么多人在回看他在空军一号上声称自己对这些

sentences.en: payments, when in fact we now know he knew everything about these payments.
sentences.zh: 付款一无所知的录像，而实际上我们现在知道他对所有这些付款了如指掌。

sentences.en: So has he lied?
sentences.zh: 所以他到底有没有撒谎？

sentences.en: Look, again, I think that's a ridiculous accusation.
sentences.zh: 听着，我再说一遍，我认为这是一个荒谬的指控。

sentences.en: The president in this matter has done nothing wrong, and there are no charges against him.
sentences.zh: 总统在这件事上没有做错任何事，他也没有面临任何指控。

sentences.en: And the Times reports that new court filings show Cohen was not the only person involved in the payoffs that resulted in his guilty plea.
sentences.zh: 《泰晤士报》报道称，新的法庭文件显示，科恩并不是唯一一个参与导致其认罪的封口费事件的人。

sentences.en: The documents show at least two executives at President Trump's company, the Trump Organization, played a role, and that Cohen
sentences.zh: 文件显示，特朗普总统的公司——特朗普集团中至少有两名高管发挥了作用，并且科恩

sentences.en: coordinated the payments with one or more members of Trump's presidential campaign.
sentences.zh: 与特朗普总统竞选团队的一个或多个成员协调了这些付款。

sentences.en: It's unclear for now whether those individuals will be charged in the case.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚这些人是否会被起诉。

sentences.en: It for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运转。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎进了一批自称为改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党便陷入了一场激烈、混乱有时又扣人心弦的权力之争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·科尼格主持的最新一期《都市》节目中，我们将讲述人们试图维持自身影响力却最终失控的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《都市》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 请在各大播客平台收听。
